finding.claim: Mail::Message.from_yaml on attacker-controlled YAML can install an attacker-chosen delivery_method object; a later deliver! runs that object's delivery code, which can append to an arbitrary path or execute an arbitrary binary.
finding.source: Untrusted YAML string passed to Mail::Message.from_yaml(str) at message.rb:1850-1851.
finding.sink: message.rb:1865-1866 instance_variable_set for any '@'-prefixed key, then message.rb:267-269 delivery_method.deliver!(self), dispatching to file_delivery.rb:34-36 File.open(path,'a') or sendmail.rb:63-80 IO.popen(command).

trace.note: safe_load with permitted_classes including Mail::Sendmail (13), Mail::Exim (14), Mail::FileDelivery (15) and Mail.delivery_method.class.
instance_variable_set sets @delivery_method to an attacker-built FileDelivery or Sendmail object with attacker-chosen settings[:location].
Path is join(settings[:location], basename(to+ext)), opened in append mode at line 36; location is unrestricted.
Alternative: settings[:location] is executed via IO.popen with an argv array (no shell) at lines 72-80, so an attacker-chosen binary runs with the message on stdin.

finding.guards_checked: safe_load restricts classes, so no arbitrary-object gadgets. Sendmail uses an argv array, not a shell. FileDelivery applies File.basename only to the recipient name, not to location. No check restricts @-keys or delivery_method values in from_yaml. Precondition: the application deserializes untrusted YAML with Message.from_yaml and then delivers. Not confirmed at runtime.

finding.claim: Attachment filenames are interpolated into a quoted Content-Disposition/Content-Type parameter without escaping ASCII quotes, semicolons or CR/LF, so an attacker-controlled filename can add header parameters or break the part header block.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled filename used as the key in mail.attachments[name] = ... (attachments_list.rb:42-43).
finding.sink: attachments_list.rb:44-46 builds 'filename="#{encoded_name}"' with no escaping; serialized at content_disposition_field.rb:34-36 and parameter_hash.rb:45-52.

trace.note: name is the caller's filename key.
decode_encode returns ASCII strings unchanged, so quotes and CR/LF pass through.
Interpolated directly into content_type, content_transfer_encoding and content_disposition strings.
ensure_filename_quoted only wraps an unquoted filename; it does not escape.
encoded uses Utilities.quote_token, which does not strip CR/LF.
dquote escapes only backslash and double quote; CR/LF are not removed.

finding.guards_checked: ContentDispositionElement re-parses the value and ParameterHash re-serializes it, which may normalize some cases. Not confirmed whether a CR/LF inside the quoted value survives parsing and serialization. Non-ASCII names are RFC2047/param-encoded and not affected. Impact is limited to MIME part headers, not top-level headers. Not verified at runtime.

finding.claim: add_file(String) and attachments[name] = {filename: path} open whatever path they are given and attach the contents; a caller passing a user-controlled path exfiltrates arbitrary local file contents into an email.
finding.source: Caller-supplied path string (message.rb:1767) or :filename hash value (attachments_list.rb:49).

trace.note: String path is opened without restriction; only File.basename is kept as the attachment name.

finding.guards_checked: No library-level restriction. This is the documented API for attaching local files, so it is an application-level precondition rather than a library bug.
